> Study Air Station is a desk air-quality monitor for students. Stuffy, polluted air makes it hard to focus, and you usually can’t tell until you feel tired or get a headache. This device measures the air around you and tells you when to act.

## Design

### 2026-11-08: I spent this session on the schematic in KiCad, starting from the Schematik desk air quality monitor as a reference. I kept the idea and redrew everything with my own pin choices.

**3h**

I spent this session on the schematic in KiCad, starting from the Schematik desk air quality monitor as a reference. I kept the idea and redrew everything with my own pin choices.

Power comes in on a screw terminal and passes through a 1N5819 diode against reverse polarity, then onto the 5 V rail. A 470 uF capacitor sits on the 5 V rail and 100 nF capacitors on 5 V and 3.3 V.

The fan is switched on the ground side by an IRLZ44N. A 100 ohm resistor sits in series with the gate and a 10k resistor pulls the gate down so the fan stays off while the ESP32 boots. A second 1N5819 across the fan absorbs the spike when it turns off.

I spent the most time on the ESP32 pins. The two buttons and the SD card MISO line use the input-only pins IO36, IO39 and IO34. Those pins have no internal pull-ups, so each button gets an external 10k pull-up. I left IO12 unused because it is a boot strapping pin. The display and the SD card share SCK and MOSI and have their own chip selects. The SCD40 uses I2C on IO21 and IO22, and the PMS5003 uses UART2 on IO16 and IO17.

I ran the electrical rules check and fixed the wires that were off the schematic grid. It now reports 0 violations. Next I’ll lay out the PCB.
